title: Scope and Identifier Resolution
definition: Scope is the region in which a binding can be referenced; identifier resolution searches the current lexical environment and then its enclosing environments until a matching binding is found or lookup fails.
purpose: Predict exactly which binding a name denotes at a given program point.
history: Lexical scope enables reasoning from source structure; exact environment and declaration rules vary by language.
mental_model: Stand at the use site and search labeled rooms from the innermost room outward; the first matching label wins.
analogy: Nested labeled drawers; useful for search direction, but unlike a runtime the drawers do not model initialization or closures.
common_mistakes: Searching by call order instead of lexical nesting
Assuming every brace creates scope for every declaration
industry_notes: Narrow scope reduces the number of locations that can read or change a binding.
ai_notes: Require AI-generated explanations to trace each lookup from the exact use site.
interview_notes: Ask candidates to resolve names in nested blocks and explain the search order.
